linkedin:
Your remote job application is being skimmed, not read. Here's how to make it impossible to ignore.

Remote hiring managers read applications on screens between meetings, often in a second language. The ones that get replies are easy to scan and clearly written for this role.

Lead with the exact job title and where you saw it. Then one sentence on why your recent work fits. Save your life story for later.

Show proof of async work: a project with written updates, a shared document you owned, or a time zone gap you handled well.

Match their words. If they say 'customer support', don't write 'client care'. Hiring software and tired humans look for the same words.

Keep your CV to one clean page. Put recent remote or freelance work first, with what you shipped, not just responsibilities.

Follow up once after a week with a short note restating your fit. More reads as pressure.

No photo unless asked. Short cover letter only if they ask a direct question. No remote experience? Point to any written, unsupervised work, paid or volunteer.

Read the full guide: http://fixtures:8000/no-numbers-post.md
